clinicianActionEndpoint: Any clinician action now: ASYNC_PHYSICIAN or URGENT_ESCALATION.

rows.message: Hi, I've had a runny nose and a mild sore throat for about 2 days. No fever, I'm still eating and drinking fine. Should I be worried?
rows.rationale: Mild, short-duration upper respiratory symptoms with no fever, normal intake, and no red flags; supportive self-care and monitoring are appropriate without clinician involvement now.

rows.message: 45M. I've had crushing pressure in the center of my chest for the last 30 minutes, it's going into my left arm and I feel sweaty and a bit sick to my stomach. I have high cholesterol.
rows.rationale: Crushing central chest pressure for 30 minutes with radiation to the left arm, diaphoresis, and nausea in a 45-year-old male with hyperlipidemia is a classic acute coronary syndrome presentation requiring immediate emergency services activation.

rows.message: 28F. It burns when I pee and I'm going a lot more often, started 2 days ago. No fever, no back pain. I'm not pregnant. I've had UTIs before.
rows.rationale: Classic uncomplicated lower UTI in a non-pregnant woman with prior similar episodes, no fever or flank pain suggesting pyelonephritis. Symptomatic and needs timely clinician review for antibiotic prescribing, but does not require in-person evaluation.

rows.message: 62F, I'm diabetic. I got a small cut on the bottom of my foot about 4 days ago and now the skin around it is red and a little swollen. No fever. It's tender when I press on it.
rows.rationale: Diabetic patient with a 4-day-old plantar foot wound showing spreading erythema, swelling, and tenderness indicates a developing diabetic foot infection. These wounds carry high risk of rapid progression to deep tissue infection, osteomyelitis, and limb loss, and require same-day in-person wound inspection, probing, possible imaging/cultures, and antibiotic initiation. Absence of fever does not exclude serious infection in diabetics.

rows.message: I've been feeling really hopeless for a few weeks now. Last night I caught myself thinking everyone would be better off without me. I don't know what to do.
rows.rationale: Weeks of hopelessness with new passive suicidal ideation ('everyone would be better off without me') is a red-flag symptom requiring same-day in-person mental health evaluation and safety assessment. No stated active plan, intent, or imminent means to warrant emergency activation, but this exceeds what async review can safely handle.

rows.message: Could I get a refill on my losartan? I've been on 50mg once a day for about 2 years, my blood pressure is well controlled, last home reading was 122/78.
rows.rationale: Routine refill request for a chronic antihypertensive with stable, well-controlled home BP and no new symptoms; requires time-sensitive async clinician review for prescribing to avoid therapy lapse.

rows.message: My 3-year-old has had a fever up to 102F for 2 days. He's still drinking okay and pretty playful in between the fevers. No rash that I can see.
rows.rationale: A 3-year-old with 2 days of fever to 102F who is well-hydrated, playful between fevers, and without rash has no red flags requiring urgent or in-person evaluation today. Routine asynchronous clinician review is appropriate to advise on antipyretic dosing, hydration, and criteria for escalation (e.g., fever beyond 5 days, poor fluid intake, decreased urine output, lethargy, rash, or difficulty breathing).

rows.message: 35F. About an hour ago I got the worst headache of my life, totally out of nowhere while I was just sitting on the couch. It hit like a thunderclap. My neck feels a bit stiff now too.
rows.rationale: Sudden thunderclap headache described as worst of life with onset at rest and new neck stiffness is a classic presentation for subarachnoid hemorrhage/meningeal irritation; requires immediate emergency evaluation with imaging.

rows.message: 30F, I'm 32 weeks pregnant. I've had a bad headache that won't go away, my vision is a little blurry, and my hands and face look puffy.
rows.rationale: 32 weeks pregnant with persistent severe headache, visual disturbance, and facial/hand edema — classic features of severe preeclampsia with risk of eclampsia, stroke, and HELLP. Requires immediate emergency obstetric evaluation, not async review.

rows.message: 50M. For a few weeks I've had pain in my upper right belly that comes and goes, usually after a fatty meal. No fever, no yellowing of my skin or eyes.
rows.rationale: Intermittent postprandial right upper quadrant pain over weeks without fever, jaundice, or acute severe pain suggests uncomplicated biliary colic; routine async review for evaluation and ultrasound ordering is appropriate.

rows.message: I have a small itchy red rash on my forearm since I did some gardening yesterday. It's not spreading and I'm breathing fine.
rows.rationale: Localized, non-spreading itchy rash after likely plant/contact exposure, with no systemic or airway symptoms. Suitable for self-care with OTC antihistamine or topical hydrocortisone and monitoring for spread or worsening.

rows.message: 68F with COPD. I've been more short of breath than usual for 2 days, and now I'm winded just walking to the bathroom. My phlegm has turned green.
rows.rationale: 68-year-old with COPD reporting 2 days of progressive dyspnea now occurring with minimal exertion (walking to bathroom) plus purulent green sputum — findings consistent with an acute COPD exacerbation, likely infective. Needs same-day in-person assessment with oxygen saturation measurement, lung exam, and consideration of steroids/antibiotics; this exceeds what async review can safely manage, but she is not describing frank respiratory failure (no confusion, cyanosis, or inability to speak) requiring immediate emergency activation.

rows.message: 55M. My right hand has been numb and tingly for a few days, worse at night. No weakness anywhere, no face drooping, my speech is normal.
rows.rationale: Several days of unilateral hand numbness/tingling worse at night suggests a peripheral compressive neuropathy (e.g., carpal tunnel) rather than acute stroke; no weakness, facial droop, or speech change reported. Routine async clinician review for evaluation and management is appropriate.

rows.message: I ate shrimp about 20 minutes ago. Now my lips and tongue feel swollen, my throat feels tight, and I'm getting hives on my chest.
rows.rationale: Rapid-onset symptoms after shellfish ingestion with lip/tongue swelling, throat tightness, and hives indicate anaphylaxis with airway involvement — requires immediate epinephrine and emergency services.

rows.message: I'd like to get tested for STIs. No symptoms, but I had a new partner recently and want to be safe.
rows.rationale: Asymptomatic patient requesting routine STI screening after a new partner; this is preventive care that can be arranged through routine asynchronous clinician review and lab ordering, with no red-flag or time-critical features.

rows.message: My 6-month-old has a fever of 100.9, she's fussy, she's had fewer wet diapers today than normal, and she doesn't seem interested in feeding.
rows.rationale: Infant under 1 year with fever plus reduced feeding and decreased wet diapers suggests early dehydration and requires same-day in-person assessment of hydration status and source of fever.

rows.message: 40M. I hurt my low back lifting something a week ago. Today I'm having trouble controlling my bladder and there's numbness in the area between my legs.
rows.rationale: New urinary retention/incontinence and saddle anesthesia one week after a lifting back injury are classic red flags for cauda equina syndrome, which requires immediate emergency evaluation and imaging to prevent permanent neurologic damage.

rows.message: Can I refill my albuterol inhaler? I use it maybe once a week, no bad attacks recently.
rows.rationale: Routine albuterol inhaler refill requires clinician prescribing assessment; patient reports stable, infrequent use (about once weekly) with no recent exacerbations or red-flag symptoms, so async review is appropriate rather than in-person or emergency care.

rows.message: I've been dizzy on and off for a few days. The room spins when I roll over or turn my head in bed, but it settles. No chest pain, no weakness, no headache.
rows.rationale: Positional vertigo lasting seconds with resolution on stillness, no neurologic red flags (no weakness, headache, chest pain), is consistent with benign paroxysmal positional vertigo and can be assessed routinely by asynchronous clinician review for confirmation and repositioning maneuver guidance.

rows.message: 70M on warfarin. I fell and hit my head yesterday. Today I have a bad headache and I've thrown up twice.
rows.rationale: Head injury while anticoagulated on warfarin, now with worsening headache and repeated vomiting — red flags for intracranial hemorrhage requiring immediate emergency evaluation and imaging.

rows.message: 55F. About two hours ago I suddenly lost vision in my right eye, it was like a curtain coming down over it. No pain at all. It hasn't come back.
rows.rationale: Sudden painless monocular vision loss described as a curtain descending, persisting for two hours, suggests retinal artery occlusion, retinal detachment, or amaurosis/stroke-related ischemia. This is a time-critical emergency requiring immediate evaluation.

rows.message: 24M. I rolled my ankle playing basketball last night. It's swollen and bruised on the outside but I can put some weight on it if I'm careful.
rows.rationale: Acute lateral ankle inversion injury with swelling and bruising but preserved weight-bearing, suggesting a likely sprain rather than fracture. Routine async review can advise RICE, bracing, and whether imaging per Ottawa ankle rules is needed; no immediate red flags (inability to bear weight, deformity, neurovascular compromise) reported.

rows.message: 60M. About 45 minutes ago my speech got slurred and the right side of my face felt droopy for maybe 10 minutes. It's back to normal now so I figured it was nothing, but wanted to check.
rows.rationale: Transient slurred speech and unilateral facial droop resolving within minutes is a likely TIA, which carries high short-term stroke risk and requires immediate emergency evaluation despite symptom resolution. Onset under an hour ago also keeps thrombolysis window relevant if symptoms recur.

rows.message: 33F. Could I get a refill on my birth control? I've been on the same one for three years with no problems.
rows.rationale: Routine oral contraceptive refill request with stable three-year use and no reported new symptoms or red flags; per refill rule, requires time-sensitive async clinician prescribing review to avoid lapse in coverage.

rows.message: 42F. I flew back from Europe two days ago and now my left calf is painful, swollen, and warm compared to the other one.
rows.rationale: Unilateral calf pain, swelling, and warmth after recent long-haul flight is highly suspicious for DVT, requiring same-day in-person evaluation with ultrasound and possible anticoagulation. No current chest pain or shortness of breath reported, so emergency activation is not indicated, but delay risks pulmonary embolism.

rows.message: 19M. Scratchy throat since yesterday, no fever, no trouble swallowing. Just annoying. Anything I can take?
rows.rationale: Mild scratchy throat for one day with no fever, no dysphagia, and no red-flag features; self-care measures such as fluids, lozenges, and OTC analgesics are appropriate without clinician involvement now.

rows.message: 70F. Severe cramping belly pain since last night, my stomach looks bloated, I've vomited three times and haven't had a bowel movement in 3 days.
rows.rationale: 70-year-old with severe cramping abdominal pain, distension, repeated vomiting, and obstipation for 3 days — classic presentation of bowel obstruction, which can progress to strangulation/perforation. Requires immediate emergency evaluation with imaging and surgical assessment.

rows.message: 29F, about 8 weeks pregnant. I started bleeding this morning, more than spotting, with cramping in my lower belly.
rows.rationale: First-trimester vaginal bleeding heavier than spotting with lower abdominal cramping requires same-day in-person evaluation (exam, hCG, ultrasound) to assess for miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy. Escalate to emergency care if heavy soaking bleeding, severe or one-sided pain, shoulder pain, fainting, or signs of shock develop.

rows.message: 45F. I had my cholesterol checked last week at a lab. Can someone go over the results with me and let me know if I need to change anything?
rows.rationale: Routine request for review and interpretation of recently completed lipid panel with no symptoms or urgency; can be handled by asynchronous clinician review at standard turnaround.

rows.message: 36M. I got into poison ivy while clearing brush on Saturday. Itchy blistery rash on both forearms, spreading a bit within that area. No fever, no trouble breathing.
rows.rationale: Localized poison ivy contact dermatitis on forearms with no fever, no facial/genital involvement, and no airway or systemic symptoms. Can be managed with OTC topical steroids, oral antihistamines, cool compresses, and washing exposed clothing/tools; escalate if rash spreads widely, involves face/eyes/genitals, or signs of infection develop.

rows.message: 50F. Bad headache since yesterday with a fever of 101.5, my neck is stiff and it hurts to look at bright light.
rows.rationale: Fever with severe headache, neck stiffness, and photophobia is a classic triad for meningitis, a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate evaluation and empiric treatment.

rows.message: My 8-year-old says her right ear has hurt since last night. No fever, she ate breakfast fine and went to school.
rows.rationale: Isolated ear pain ~1 day in a well-appearing child with no fever, normal appetite, and attending school. No red flags (no mastoid swelling, neck stiffness, severe systemic illness), so routine async clinician review for possible otitis media evaluation and management is appropriate.

rows.message: 65M, type 2 diabetes. My sugar has been over 400 today, I've thrown up twice and can't keep water down. I feel awful.
rows.rationale: Type 2 diabetic with glucose >400, repeated vomiting and inability to tolerate oral fluids — concern for DKA/hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state with dehydration. Needs immediate emergency evaluation for IV fluids, labs, and insulin therapy.

rows.message: 27F. My seasonal allergies are back — sneezing, itchy eyes, stuffy nose. What over the counter option do you recommend?
rows.rationale: Typical mild seasonal allergic rhinitis symptoms (sneezing, itchy eyes, nasal congestion) with no red flags such as wheezing, shortness of breath, or fever. This can be managed with OTC options like a non-sedating oral antihistamine, intranasal steroid spray, and antihistamine eye drops; no clinician task is required now.

rows.message: 58M. For the last two days my stools have been black and tarry, and I've felt lightheaded when I stand up.
rows.rationale: Melena for two days with orthostatic lightheadedness suggests active upper GI bleeding with possible hemodynamic compromise; this requires immediate emergency evaluation.

rows.message: 31F. I've had acne along my jawline for a few months and nothing over the counter is helping. Would like to talk about options.
rows.rationale: Chronic, non-urgent acne unresponsive to OTC treatment; suitable for routine asynchronous clinician review to discuss prescription options. No red-flag or time-sensitive features.

rows.message: 44M. Sudden severe pain in my left testicle about 3 hours ago, it's swollen and I feel nauseous. Pain isn't letting up.
rows.rationale: Sudden severe unilateral testicular pain with swelling and nausea for 3 hours is classic for testicular torsion, a surgical emergency with a narrow window (~6 hours) to preserve the testicle. Requires immediate emergency evaluation with urgent ultrasound and urology involvement.

rows.message: 22F. Following up on my ankle sprain from last week — it's improving. Just wondering how much ibuprofen I can safely take and for how long.
rows.rationale: Improving ankle sprain with no red flags; question is routine OTC analgesic dosing guidance that can be addressed with self-care education.

rows.message: 39F, two weeks postpartum. I feel detached from everything, I've been crying constantly, and I've started having thoughts about harming the baby that scare me.
rows.rationale: Two weeks postpartum with detachment, constant crying, and intrusive thoughts of harming the infant raises concern for postpartum psychosis/severe postpartum depression — a psychiatric emergency requiring immediate in-person evaluation and infant safety assurance.

rows.message: 47M. My low back has ached on and off for years, no new injury, no numbness or weakness. I'd like a referral for physical therapy.
rows.rationale: Chronic, stable mechanical low back pain with no red flags (no new injury, no neurologic deficits); request for a PT referral can be handled by routine asynchronous clinician review.

rows.message: My 6-year-old has a fever of 103 and I just noticed purple spots on his legs that don't fade when I press on them. He seems very sleepy.
rows.rationale: Child with high fever, non-blanching purpuric rash, and lethargy — classic red flags for meningococcal sepsis/meningitis. Requires immediate emergency evaluation (call emergency services/ED now).

rows.message: 52F. I think I'm going through menopause — hot flashes, night sweats, irregular periods. I'd like to discuss what my options are.
rows.rationale: Typical perimenopausal symptoms without red flags; routine asynchronous clinician review is appropriate to discuss management options such as hormonal or non-hormonal therapy.

rows.message: 34M. I've had a cough for about three weeks now with night sweats and I've lost maybe 10 pounds without trying. I moved here from a country where TB is common.
rows.rationale: Three weeks of cough with night sweats, unintentional 10-lb weight loss, and epidemiologic risk from a high-TB-burden region strongly suggests active pulmonary tuberculosis. This requires same-day in-person evaluation with chest imaging and sputum testing, plus airborne isolation precautions to limit transmission. Not an immediate emergency absent hemoptysis, severe breathlessness, or hemodynamic instability.

rows.message: 68M. Both my ankles have been swelling for a couple weeks and it's gotten worse. The last two nights I've had to sit up to breathe because lying flat makes me short of breath.
rows.rationale: 68-year-old with two weeks of worsening bilateral ankle edema plus new orthopnea/paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea suggests decompensating heart failure. He needs same-day in-person evaluation (exam, vitals/oxygen saturation, ECG, chest imaging, labs) rather than async review; no report of resting severe dyspnea, chest pain, or syncope that would mandate immediate emergency activation, though worsening symptoms would escalate that need.

rows.message: 25F. I got my STI panel results in the portal and I don't understand what one of the values means. Can someone explain?
rows.rationale: Request is for interpretation of already-available lab results with no symptoms or urgency described; routine asynchronous clinician review and explanation is appropriate.

rows.message: 30M. Requesting a refill of my finasteride, 1mg daily. No side effects, been on it about a year.
rows.rationale: Routine medication refill request for finasteride with no reported side effects or red-flag symptoms; requires time-sensitive async prescribing review per refill policy.

rows.message: 45F. I've had trouble falling asleep for the last month or so. Work has been stressful. I'm functioning but tired all day.
rows.rationale: One month of stress-related initial insomnia with daytime fatigue but preserved functioning and no red flags; routine async review for sleep hygiene/CBT-I guidance and evaluation of contributing factors is appropriate.

rows.message: 71F. I fell in the kitchen this morning and my right hip hurts badly. I can't put any weight on that leg.
rows.rationale: Elderly patient with fall and hip pain with inability to bear weight suggests possible hip fracture, requiring same-day in-person evaluation with imaging.

rows.message: 28M. Sharp pain on the left side of my chest since yesterday, worse when I take a deep breath. I did a heavy chest workout two days ago. No shortness of breath, no leg swelling, I don't smoke.
rows.rationale: Young patient with localized, reproducible pleuritic/musculoskeletal chest pain following heavy chest exercise, without dyspnea, leg swelling, or smoking/other thrombotic risk factors. No red flags suggesting ACS or PE, so routine async clinician review is appropriate to confirm musculoskeletal cause and advise on analgesia.

rows.message: 40F. My usual migraine started this morning — same one-sided throbbing and light sensitivity I always get. I'm out of sumatriptan and would like a refill.
rows.rationale: Refill request for sumatriptan with a typical, previously established migraine pattern and no new or red-flag features; needs time-sensitive async prescribing review so treatment can be taken during the current attack.
